classification.classification_note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports a 4-byte READ in `xmlStaticCopyNode()` reached from `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt()`. Source analysis shows that XInclude text processing caches a reader-owned `xmlNodePtr` in `ctxt->txtTab`, the XML reader later frees that node, and a later duplicate text include reloads the dangling pointer for `xmlCopyNode()`.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in XInclude processing: xmlXIncludeLoadTxt (xinclude.c) can end up calling xmlStaticCopyNode (tree.c) on a node that has already been freed (by the XML reader code), resulting in a read of freed heap memory. An attacker-controlled XML with XInclude can trigger this, causing crashes, memory corruption, or potentially enabling information disclosure or further exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged XML reaches the XInclude reader path and contains two `xinclude:include` elements with the same `href` `../ents/isolatin.txt` and `parse="text"`. On the first include, `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt()` allocates a text node for that external text resource and `xmlXIncludeAddTxt()` stores the live `xmlNodePtr` in `ctxt->txtTab` instead of copying stable text content. When the reader advances, `xmlTextReaderRead()` unlinks that earlier included text sibling and `xmlTextReaderFreeNodeList()` frees the node, but `ctxt->txtTab` still retains the pointer. When the later duplicate include is processed, `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt()` finds the cached URL match and calls `xmlCopyNode(ctxt->txtTab[i], 1)` on the freed node, and the saved crash occurs when `xmlStaticCopyNode()` reads `node->type`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled XInclude target. The witnessed XML supplies the same `href` `../ents/isolatin.txt` on two `xinclude:include` elements, and this value drives both the initial cache insertion and the later cache-hit reuse.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the XML witness used in Stage 01. Its visible trigger semantics are two `xinclude:include` elements in the XInclude namespace, each with `href="../ents/isolatin.txt"` and `parse="text"`.

sink.description: Crash sink. `xmlCopyNode()` passes the dangling cached pointer into `xmlStaticCopyNode()`, which immediately reads the freed node's `type` field and triggers the saved heap-use-after-free READ.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. The XInclude text cache stores a borrowed `xmlNodePtr` owned by the reader instead of copying durable text data, so `ctxt->txtTab` can outlive the node and later hold a dangling pointer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later stale pointer use is keyed by attacker-controlled XInclude attributes first read here: the duplicate `href` chooses the cache entry, and the paired `parse="text"` attribute keeps execution on the text-caching path.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admission gate. The staged XML is not just well-formed; it reaches the reader branch that recognizes an element in the XInclude namespace and routes it into XInclude processing.

coarse_trace.summary: The witness reaches the XInclude reader branch, so elements in the XInclude namespace are expanded and processed by the XInclude engine.
The first `parse="text"` include loads `../ents/isolatin.txt`, allocates a text node, and caches the live `xmlNodePtr` plus its URL in `ctxt->txtTab` and `ctxt->txturlTab`.
As the reader advances, it unlinks the earlier included text sibling and frees the underlying `xmlNode`, leaving the cached pointer in `ctxt->txtTab` dangling.
The later duplicate text include canonicalizes the same URL, matches the cached URL entry, and reloads the dangling pointer with `xmlCopyNode(ctxt->txtTab[i], 1)`.
The copy routine dereferences the freed node at `switch (node->type)`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ.

fine_trace.note: Source. Each XInclude element materializes its attacker-controlled target here. In the witnessed XML, both include elements supply the same `href` `../ents/isolatin.txt`.
The witness also materializes `parse="text"`, and this branch sets `xml = 0` so the include is handled by the text-specific caching path instead of document inclusion.
Because `xml == 0`, XInclude dispatches this include into `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt()`, the only path that populates `ctxt->txtTab` for cached text includes.
The first text include allocates a fresh `xmlNode` to hold the referenced text resource. The saved allocation stack identifies this statement as the origin of the later-freed object.
Root cause. The cache retains the live reader-owned `xmlNodePtr` together with a durable copy of its URL, so later URL matches can reload this pointer after the reader has freed the node itself.

After the first include has been inserted and the reader advances, cleanup selects the previous sibling as `tmp`. On the witnessed path that sibling is the first included text node whose address is still cached in `ctxt->txtTab`.
The reader actually frees the text node's heap allocation here. No corresponding cleanup removes the alias from `ctxt->txtTab`, so that cache entry becomes dangling.

When the later duplicate include is processed, the same attacker-controlled `href` is canonicalized into `URL` again. On the witness this produces the same text-include URL that was stored in `ctxt->txturlTab` earlier.

The duplicate include takes the cache-hit branch because its canonical URL matches the stored URL for the first include. That branch bypasses reloading the text resource and reuses the cached pointer entry.
The cache-hit path reloads the dangling pointer from `ctxt->txtTab[i]` and passes it into the node-copy routine as if it were still live.
Sink. `xmlStaticCopyNode()` immediately dereferences the freed node to read `node->type`, which matches the saved 4-byte heap-use-after-free READ in the sanitizer trace.

poc.trigger: Run the staged XML witness through `fuzz/xml`; the witnessed path processes two `parse="text"` XInclude elements for the same `href` `../ents/isolatin.txt`, frees the first included text node during reader cleanup, then reuses that cached pointer on the later duplicate include.

format.name: XML document with duplicate XInclude text references
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are an XML document that reaches the XInclude namespace handling path and contains two `xinclude:include` elements with identical `href` `../ents/isolatin.txt` and `parse="text"`. The first include must populate `ctxt->txtTab`; the later duplicate include must hit the cached URL entry after the reader has already freed the original text node.
